subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If y = x√(a² + x²) + a² log(x + √(a² + x²)), prove that dy/dx = 2√(a² + x²).

mark_split.label: Write the derivative of the square root
Differentiate the first term by the product rule
Combine the first term into one fraction
Add the two parts and simplify

The split follows the shape this bank uses for a Maths-1B Section C question, cut on the moves this working takes and weighted so that the two places where something genuinely cancels — the logarithm term and the final cancellation — carry two marks each. Unlike the other Section-C questions in this chapter, this one uses no logarithmic differentiation: it is the product rule and the chain rule, and the logarithm is part of the function rather than a method. The mathematics was checked independently before writing: with a = 2, the result 2√(a² + x²) agrees with a central difference quotient of the given function at x = 1 (4.472135955), at x = 3 (7.211102551) and at x = −1.5 (5.000000000), to nine decimal places at all three points. steps.label: Write the derivative of the square root
steps.margin_note: First mark. This one derivative is used twice, once in each term, so writing it out at the top saves repeating the chain rule later. No logarithmic differentiation is needed anywhere in this question.
steps.memory_tip: The derivative of √(a² + x²) is x over the same root. The root reappears underneath, never squared.

steps.label: Differentiate the first term by the product rule
steps.margin_note: Two marks. x√(a² + x²) is a product of two functions of x, so the product rule applies: derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second.
steps.memory_tip: First stays, second differentiates; second stays, first differentiates. Here that gives the root itself plus x times (1).

steps.why: This cancellation is what makes the logarithm term short. Without it the term stays a fraction with x + √(a² + x²) in the denominator; with it, the term reduces to a single fraction over the same root as the first term, ready to be added.

steps.label: Add the two parts and simplify
steps.margin_note: The last two marks, and they are for the cancellation, not for writing the answer down. Both parts already sit over the same root, so the tops add to 2a² + 2x² = 2(a² + x²), and 2(a² + x²) divided by √(a² + x²) is 2√(a² + x²).
steps.memory_tip: A quantity divided by its own square root gives that square root back: (a² + x²)/√(a² + x²) = √(a² + x²).
